description:
## Question

defk runs the C compiler on the build machine at compile time. The verdict's go/no-go rule (see "What must docs/verdict.md contain to count as done?") requires this stance to be settled: is a C toolchain at build time an acceptable requirement for a defk library (as for elixir_make packages), or does a library need a named way out (precompiled artefacts, a bundled compiler, a Cranelift JIT path, defk-o1w)? What does each option cost, and what goes in the verdict's Limitations?

comments.text:
Resolution: a C toolchain at build time is acceptable, stated per audience in the verdict. (a) App developers writing their own kernels: acceptable, same requirement as elixir_make packages (bcrypt_elixir, exqlite); a limit, not a blocker for go/no-go. (b) Hex library authors shipping kernels: the named way out is precompiled artefacts in the cc_precompiler / rustler_precompiled style (built per target in CI, downloaded and checked by hash; defk's hash-keyed build cache fits this), named in the verdict only, nothing built in this map. A bundled compiler (Zigler-style) is rejected; Cranelift JIT (defk-o1w) stays a P4 exploration listed under 'Where defk could grow', not the way out. (c) Livebook users: need Xcode CLT / build-essential, stated in the guide.

Evidence: an actionable missing-compiler error in the agreed error format, plus honouring ERTS_INCLUDE_DIR ([Actionable error when no C compiler is found](defk-lb8)); one recorded mix release build in a stock Debian Elixir image ([Record a mix release build in a stock Debian Elixir image](defk-ds0)).

Cross-compilation (Nerves, macOS -> Linux) is out of scope for building; listed under Limitations as untested.

Verdict Limitations gets three lines: C toolchain needed at build time (as elixir_make); library authors would need a precompilation step that doesn't exist yet (cc_precompiler as the model); cross-compiling and untested architectures unverified.

This settles go/no-go condition (d) in 'What must docs/verdict.md contain to count as done?'.

title: Is a C compiler at build time acceptable for a defk library?
